samples.summary: Untrusted clipboard content is promoted to "internal paste" by a bare string-equality check against a copy buffer that now survives every paste
samples.evidence: `if (this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text)` (sheet.ts:2243) is the only thing distinguishing data that originated inside this sheet from data supplied by the OS clipboard, i.e. by any other application or web page the user copied from. Everything downstream of that branch treats the payload as trusted internal state: it discards the clipboard text entirely and writes `this.copyBuffer.grid` (relocated formulas, sheet.ts:2245), applies `copyBuffer.rangeStyles`, and now — new in this change — mutates the merge map via `planPasteMerges`/`applyPasteMerges`, deleting destination merged blocks (`store.deleteMerge`, sheet.ts:2541) and, for a cut, deleting the recorded source range (sheet.ts:2356-2366). This change widens the window for that confusion in two ways: (a) both view paste paths no longer call `clearCopyBuffer()` (view/worksheet.ts:4947, view/spreadsheet.ts:728), so a copy buffer now persists for the whole session until Escape or the next copy, instead of one paste; (b) the consequences of a mismatch grew from "wrong values/formulas" to "merged blocks created and destroyed". Attack shape: an attacker who can influence or predict what the victim copies externally (short or attacker-authored payloads such as `10`, a single word, or a row the attacker wrote into a shared/collab sheet) gets the victim's paste to silently apply the stale internal buffer — including merge deletions — rather than the clipboard they actually copied. I could not demonstrate a practical way to force byte-equality against an unknown buffer, hence low confidence, but the trust decision itself is content equality on attacker-reachable input with no nonce/identity token (e.g. a clipboard-embedded random id, or `text/html` origin marker) binding the clipboard to this buffer.

samples.summary: Copied cell contents (values, formulas, styles) are now retained in memory indefinitely instead of being dropped after the paste
samples.evidence: Both view paste paths dropped their `this.sheet.clearCopyBuffer()` call (view/worksheet.ts:4947, view/spreadsheet.ts:728). `copyBuffer` holds a full snapshot of the copied region — `grid` (cell values and formula source), `rangeStyles`, `text` and now `merges` (sheet.ts:373-382) — and is only released on Escape (view/worksheet.ts:5117-5118), on the next copy/cut, or when a cut is consumed (sheet.ts:2286). Copied data may be exactly the sensitive content of the sheet (credentials pasted into a cell, PII), and it now lingers for the session in the page's heap, where any XSS or a heap/memory dump broadens the exposure relative to the previous behaviour. This is a retention/hardening concern, not an exploit on its own; if the persistence is wanted for repeat pastes, consider clearing the buffer on blur/visibility loss or after a timeout.

samples.summary: clearCellsUnderMerge performs one unbatched async store read per covered cell with no bound on the merge span, now reachable repeatedly from paste
samples.evidence: `clearCellsUnderMerge` iterates `this.mergeCoveredSrefs(anchor, span)` and issues `await this.store.get(ref)` per covered sref (sheet.ts:2572-2578), plus nested per-ghost `store.get`/`store.delete` loops. `span` comes from the copy buffer and is only limited by what `mergeSelection` allowed, which can be a whole-sheet/whole-column selection, so the loop is effectively unbounded (millions of awaited store round-trips) and runs inside the paste batch, freezing the tab. Before this change the loop was only reachable from a drag-move gesture (the code was relocated out of `moveRangeTo`); it is now also reachable from paste, and because the copy buffer is no longer cleared after a paste, the same oversized merge can be replayed with repeated Ctrl+V. A malicious collaborator in a shared document can plant a very large merged block for the victim to copy/paste. Client-side availability only, hence minor.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is genuinely present (sheet.ts:2243 `text === this.copyBuffer.text`; merge mutation via planPasteMerges/applyPasteMerges at 2258 and 2332; cut source deletion at 2356-2366; clearCopyBuffer() removal documented at view/worksheet.ts:4941-4947 and view/spreadsheet.ts:724-728), so this is not `not-present`. It is, however, out of the Security lens's lane. (1) The data flow is inverted from the finding's headline: in the matched branch the clipboard `text` is used only as an equality key and is then discarded — sheet.ts:2245-2265 reads exclusively from `this.copyBuffer` — so no untrusted byte reaches any sink (no injection, no deserialization, no traversal). (2) The comparison is not a permission gate: both branches write to the same `destStart` with the same authority, behind the same readOnly/pivot gating (sheet.ts:2217, view/spreadsheet.ts:699), so a false match yields no privilege gain and no cross-tenant access; `copyBuffer` (sheet.ts:380-387) is populated only by this user's own copy()/cut() (sheet.ts:2149-2185) on this same Sheet instance, so nothing attacker-controlled is written. (3) Every call site of Sheet.paste is a client-side, user-gesture clipboard read (view/worksheet.ts:4947, view/spreadsheet.ts:728, frontend sheet-view.tsx:776) — there is no remote or collaboration channel supplying `text`/`html`. (4) `copyBuffer.text` is not a credential or MAC, so the non-constant-time `===` is not a crypto weakness. The residual impact — a paste applying a stale internal buffer, including merge create/delete — is a visible, undoable data-integrity/wrong-branch bug in the user's own local document, which is the correctness lens's lane (explicitly deferred by this rubric, and already covered under .agent-review/correctness for the clearCopyBuffer removal).
